rounds.text: NDR Auto Components demonstrates exceptional long-term momentum, highlighted by a 5-year sales CAGR of 48% [E14] and profit CAGR of 49% [E17], while generating return metrics such as an ROCE of 22.2% [E12] and ROE of 18.9% [E13] that far exceed sector benchmarks of 12.62% [E10] and 11.57% [E9]. This operational expansion is grounded in a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17x [E34] and operating cash flow of Rs 37 Cr [E31], alongside a 32.1% drop in capital work-in-progress indicating completed capex with new capacity coming online [E37]. Despite recent profit growth exceeding 1-year share price growth by 34% [E54], the stock remains significantly under-appreciated; the current market price of Rs 817 reflects a 26.7% margin of safety against its DCF intrinsic value of Rs 1115 per share [E42, E43], and a reverse DCF shows the market is pricing in only 13.7% earnings growth versus the base case assumption of 18.0% [E44]. Conceded: the business displays near-term friction, as evidenced by a 1-year share price growth of -16% [E22], a negative free cash flow of Rs -36 Cr in Mar 2026 [E32], borrowings rising to Rs 62 Cr [E36], and a P/B of 5.39x well above the sector benchmark of 2.79x [E7]. Nevertheless, with the stock sitting at just 36% of its 52-week range [E5] and scoring 78 out of 100 on rules-based screens [E57], current levels fail to reflect an enterprise with accelerating earnings growth [E61] and positive institutional money flow [E41].
